title: Singular partitive: -ta/-tä
summary: Add -ta/-tä to the unchanged base in these selected words ending in two vowels or a consonant: maa (“country”) → maata.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.
Add -ta/-tä to the unchanged base in these two-vowel and consonant-ending words. Vowel harmony selects the final a/ä. This is a selected family, not a rule for every consonant-ending noun.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: maa + ta = maata; keep both a vowels in the base.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “country”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
puu + ta = puuta; keep both u vowels.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “tree”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
tee has only neutral vowels, so tee + tä = teetä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “tea”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
työ has front vowels, so työ + tä = työtä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “work”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
radio + ta = radiota; keep the final io.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “radio”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
televisio contains back vowel o: televisio + ta = televisiota.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “television”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Add -ta directly to the consonant-ending base: puhelin + ta = puhelinta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “telephone”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
avain + ta = avainta; this singular form keeps n.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “key”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Keep the long vowel in maa, puu and tee.
Do not substitute a plural form when the requested form is singular.
